Docs note added by #324 (apps/docs/content/preset/core.mdx, since replaced): "Certain rules are disabled because they are too slow to run with the Scanner. As noted in the [Biome docs](https://biomejs.dev/guides/investigate-slowness/#first-things-first), project rules enabled are known to cause performance overhead in return for more advanced analysis. In our testing, we have found these rules can make the difference between a 300ms and a 13s lint." Why a separate preset rather than a runtime skip: #606 (7.3.0 made a direct `biome check` go from 1.3s to 4s); maintainer: "it's a Biome project domain issue related to how we implemented #445" and "If you upgrade to 7.3.1 the Biome scanner rules have been re-disabled by default and we've found a different way to enable them". f84edfff docs: "Since the rules are baked into your Biome config, they work in both the CLI and your IDE automatically — no runtime flags needed." The 2026-07-04 allowlist had two unrelated entries (sonarjs/no-reference-error, unicorn/number-literal-case).
parityScript.coverage: Compares Oxlint core+js-plugins (+framework) with ESLint core+type-aware (+framework) only. Biome is 'aligned manually — it is not covered here' (header). oxc/* and react-doctor/* are skipped in the Oxlint->ESLint direction. ESLint-enabled rules Oxlint can't run are only counted as informational 'gaps': here import-x/no-relative-packages, import-x/no-useless-path-segments, import-x/no-restricted-paths, unicorn/no-barrel-files, unicorn/no-useless-re-export. Options are compared only when the Oxlint preset spells some out; none of these Oxlint rules do. Because js-plugins is always included, the core-only Oxlint gap on sonarjs/no-wildcard-import is never flagged.

docsMentions.text: 'Rules that read type information, or scan the whole project, are slower than the rest and need more setup, so every linter keeps them out of `core`.'

'The `type-aware` preset enables project-graph and type-aware rules: `noPrivateImports`, `noUnresolvedImports`, `noImportCycles`, `noDeprecatedImports`, `useJsonImportAttributes`, and `useArraySortCompare`. These rules require Biome's scanner, so they're slower and shipped as a separate layer:'

'For Biome, `--type-aware` adds the `ultracite/biome/type-aware` preset to your Biome config's `extends` array. This enables the project/scanner rules `noPrivateImports`, `noUnresolvedImports`, `noImportCycles`, `noDeprecatedImports`, `useJsonImportAttributes`, and `useArraySortCompare`.' L96: 'Since the rules are baked into your Biome config, they work in both the CLI and your IDE automatically — no runtime flags needed.'

FAQ: 'add the `type-aware` preset, whose 6 rules need Biome to scan the whole project first: `noPrivateImports`, `noUnresolvedImports`, `noImportCycles`, `noDeprecatedImports`, `useJsonImportAttributes` and `useArraySortCompare`.'

'The `type-aware` preset adds rules like `noImportCycles`, `noUnresolvedImports` and `noDeprecatedImports`. They need Biome to scan your whole project first, so they’re opt-in: `init --type-aware` adds the preset.' L117: rules 'catch what agents get wrong: barrel files, nested ternaries, awaits inside loops and forEach where for…of would do.'

'Enforcing Path Aliases' recipe: '`import/no-relative-parent-imports` is a native Oxlint rule: it flags `../` in imports, type imports, and re-exports at any depth, while still allowing `./sibling` imports within a directory.' plus a no-restricted-imports pattern variant (L154-170).
project-specific rules 'such as `no-restricted-imports` paths' are not carried over
No page explains import/no-cycle, import-x/no-cycle, oxc/no-barrel-file, sonarjs/no-wildcard-import or unicorn/no-barrel-files.

inconsistencies.detail: Oxlint core: import/no-cycle error (core L263). ESLint core: import-x/no-cycle error (effective [2] on .ts/.js/.tsx). Biome core: noImportCycles off (core L548); error only in the opt-in biome/type-aware preset (L16). A Biome user on the default setup gets no cycle check; Oxlint and ESLint users do.

inconsistencies.topic: Docs claim vs presets on whole-project rules
inconsistencies.detail: configuration.mdx L41 says rules that 'scan the whole project ... every linter keeps them out of `core`', but import/no-cycle (Oxlint) and import-x/no-cycle (ESLint) build a module graph and run in core, and Biome's project rule noUndeclaredDependencies moved into Biome core in v8 (#843).

The maintainer's #843 timing (2026-10-11, Biome 2.5.15, one 1,244-file project) put core + the whole type-aware preset at 915 ms vs 864 ms for core, and moved noUndeclaredDependencies to core on that basis; noImportCycles stayed opt-in with no recorded reason. Its own cost was not measured separately (useArraySortCompare, also in type-aware, is the rule #768 measured as up to ~260x slower).

inconsistencies.topic: What counts as a type-only import in cycle detection
inconsistencies.detail: Biome noImportCycles ignoreTypes (default on) skips only `import type`, not `import { type Foo }` (schema text). import-x/no-cycle skips both `import type` and declarations whose specifiers are all `type`. Oxlint's ignoreTypes defaults to true; which forms it treats as type-only was not checked. The same cycle through inline type specifiers can be reported by Biome and not by ESLint.

Oxlint core: import/no-namespace off, and nothing else in core reports it. ESLint core: import-x/no-namespace off, but sonarjs/no-wildcard-import is on (effective [2]) and reports every ImportNamespaceSpecifier. Biome core: noNamespaceImport error (plus noDynamicNamespaceImportAccess). Oxlint reports it only with the opt-in js-plugins preset (sonarjs/no-wildcard-import, L426). The agent rules tell every user 'Prefer specific imports over namespace imports'.

Biome core: noReExportAll off. ESLint core: every `export * from` is reported by sonarjs/no-wildcard-import (ExportAllDeclaration), and unicorn/no-barrel-files reports files that are only re-exports. Oxlint core: allowed unless one file re-exports more than 100 modules through `export *` (oxc/no-barrel-file default threshold); Oxlint js-plugins reports it via sonarjs. So the same `export * from './x'` fails ESLint core, passes Oxlint core, and passes Biome core unless noBarrelFile flags the file (Biome's noBarrelFile semantics not checked here).

Three different definitions are on: Biome noBarrelFile (error, no options); ESLint unicorn/no-barrel-files (since 2026-08-19, any file made only of imports and re-exports, no threshold); Oxlint oxc/no-barrel-file (only past 100 `export *` modules by default, named re-exports not counted). ESLint has no oxc/no-barrel-file and Oxlint has no unicorn/no-barrel-files, and the parity script skips oxc/* and lists unicorn/no-barrel-files only as an informational gap. The agent rules say 'Avoid barrel files (index files that re-export everything)', which Oxlint core will almost never enforce.

ESLint: only in the eslint/react preset. Oxlint: in js-plugins, which applies to every file of any project that extends it (React Doctor marks the rule framework 'global'). An Oxlint js-plugins user without React gets it; an ESLint user without the react preset does not. React Doctor itself ships it defaultEnabled false; Ultracite sets error in both.

Both were turned off together on 2024-12-10 (7616c187, next-forge alignment); #233 (2025-08-16) turned only noBarrelFile back on. No recorded reason keeps noReExportAll off, while ESLint core effectively bans `export *` via sonarjs/no-wildcard-import.

import-x/no-relative-packages, import-x/no-useless-path-segments, unicorn/no-useless-re-export and unicorn/no-barrel-files are on in ESLint core with no Oxlint 1.86.0 implementation and no Biome counterpart configured. Biome-only: noDynamicNamespaceImportAccess, noExportedImports.

Oxlint no-restricted-imports, ESLint no-restricted-imports and import-x/no-restricted-paths, and Biome noRestrictedImports are all on with no paths, patterns or zones, so none can report anything. Consistent across linters, but each preset lists them as 'error'.

inconsistencies.topic: Historical: Oxlint vs ESLint on ../ imports
inconsistencies.detail: From V7 (2025-12-28) to 2026-03-14 Oxlint core reported every `../` import (import/no-relative-parent-imports via the restriction category) while ESLint has had the rule off since 2022.

inconsistencies.topic: Historical: ESLint cycle check missed whole file types
inconsistencies.detail: From V7 (2025-12-28) to 2026-09-28 (8f236ee3) ESLint core did not lint .tsx/.jsx (framework rules only) or .mts/.cts (no matching config), so import-x/no-cycle never ran on them, while Oxlint checked all of them.

inconsistencies.topic: Historical: agent rules vs Biome on cycles
inconsistencies.detail: From v5 (2025-06-22) to 2025-10-20 the generated rules said 'Prevent import cycles.' while Biome's noImportCycles was off. Since 2025-10-20 the template says nothing about cycles, though Oxlint and ESLint core enforce them.

inconsistencies.topic: Two ESLint rules leave no clean re-export
inconsistencies.detail: Within ESLint core, `export { default } from 'pkg'` trips unicorn/no-barrel-files and `import x from 'pkg'; export default x` trips unicorn/prefer-export-from (and is also a barrel), so init's stylelint config has to spread the object (`export default { ...config }`; src/linters/stylelint.ts L42-46, eb13a45b).

notes: Recorded rationales exist only for: Biome noBarrelFile (#233), Biome noImportCycles being off in core / living in type-aware (v5 comment, #324, #445, #606, f84edfff docs), ESLint import-x/no-unused-modules off (ESLint 10 no-op), the Oxlint js-plugins move (cost; #742, d186c53c, 5da879b3), and the core declining layout-specific import restrictions (#782). Nothing records why import/no-cycle or import-x/no-cycle is on, why import/no-namespace or max-dependencies are off, why noReExportAll is off, or why the agent template has its barrel and namespace lines.
Cycle-rule options have never been set anywhere: no maxDepth, ignoreExternal, ignoreTypes or allowUnsafeDynamicCyclicDependency in any config path in the history.

The only rule-level performance number on record for a cycle rule is #139 (2024-06-29): import/no-cycle 160.265 ms, 19.9% of lint time on one file under ESLint. For Biome the numbers are for the scanner rules as a group: '300ms and a 13s lint' (#324 docs note), 1.3s -> 4s (#606), 864 -> 915 ms for the whole type-aware preset (#843).

The 2026-04-23 changelog rewrite (7748b21d) added retroactive entries (4.1.9 'Sync ... with the ruleset used by next-forge', 5.1.9 '#233', 6.0.0 'c5c7ca1 ... noImportCycles ...'). The 6.0.0 entry wrongly says c5c7ca1 disabled noImportCycles; it had been off since v5.

ESLint import resolver: settings { node: true, typescript: true } since 2023-01-14 (f89fb4de), removed with ESLint in 2024-07, restored in V7, renamed import-x/* on 2026-03-14 (acf301cd). eslint-import-resolver-typescript is a dependency since 2023-04-16 (2071f80e) and is what init installs today.
